preregistration.question: Can coupled-edit selectors improve deterministic TSTR utility over one-at-a-time selection when all methods share the same candidate pool, whole-file byte cap, and evaluation budget?

controls.optimization_compute: same maximum deterministic evaluator calls per selector
controls.size_measure: serialized complete artifact bytes for each selected edit set; no sum of marginal byte estimates
controls.critical_tail_gate: reject any candidate below the preregistered critical-tail TSTR floor even when aggregate TSTR improves

external_campaign.reason: W04 and W03 native runtimes are not yet qualified; no external campaign result or selector benefit claim is admitted

deterministic_fixtures.interpretation: In this deterministic XOR interaction fixture, single edits score below the empty baseline. Beam, exchange, and lookahead discover the pair; one-step greedy and the independent additive section baseline do not. This is a unit fixture, not measured model performance.

deterministic_fixtures.observed: Every searching selector rejects the paired candidate and retains the empty baseline despite its aggregate win.

deterministic_fixtures.measurement: Serialize base bytes and the complete canonically ordered edit set, then measure the resulting byte vector length.
deterministic_fixtures.observed: The pair's measured byte delta differs from the sum of its two isolated deltas because shared serialization framing is counted once.

limits: Synthetic deterministic objectives do not establish real TSTR improvement.
Native W04/W03 qualification and an externally pinned model panel remain prerequisites for campaign admission.
Empirical TSTR and critical-tail checks are not formal differential privacy or HIPAA de-identification claims.
